context.title: Why the ontology is inconsistent
context.text:
Reasoner: HermiT.
The ontology is inconsistent: as it stands, nothing can satisfy all of it.
Justification 1 (the axioms that together force it):
  'funghi price' 'has value' "9.50"^^xsd:decimal
  'has value' Range: xsd:float
Note (OWL 2): xsd:decimal and xsd:float have disjoint value spaces: "9.50"^^xsd:decimal is not an xsd:float. The reasoner applies this.
Justification 2 (the axioms that together force it):
  'has value' Range: xsd:float
  'margherita price' 'has value' "8.50"^^xsd:decimal
Note (OWL 2): xsd:decimal and xsd:float have disjoint value spaces: "8.50"^^xsd:decimal is not an xsd:float. The reasoner applies this.
Justification 3 (the axioms that together force it):
  'has value' Range: xsd:float
  'hawaiian price' 'has value' "10.00"^^xsd:decimal
Note (OWL 2): xsd:decimal and xsd:float have disjoint value spaces: "10.00"^^xsd:decimal is not an xsd:float. The reasoner applies this.

message: Why is the ontology inconsistent? Explain the justification in plain language, and say which axiom is most likely the mistake. Then propose the repair as an ontoboard-proposal block: action: remove-axiom when an axiom of the justification is wrong, or action: replace-axiom when it is right in spirit but wrong in a detail (a range, a quantifier, a class), with the axiom copied exactly as the justification shows it.
